1) set beta = 0 disabling kv_divergence

Hello，could you explain the update parameters?

1) set beta = 0 disabling kv_divergene.

- Setting beta = 0 effectively removes this KL divergence penalty (as I see in your blog posts).
- So, I have enabled to set beta = 0.0 in .sh file, and when beta is set to 0.0, no reference model is initialized (which significantly reduces GPU usage during the GRPO training).


2) Add Clip Higher from DAPO:
- This change directly implements one of the core techniques introduced in the DAPO paper, specifically designed to promote exploration and prevent "entropy collapse" (where the model becomes too conservative and produces non-diverse outputs).

- Standard policy gradient methods often "clip" the objective function to limit how large the policy updates can be. 
- DAPO modifies this by using a higher upper clipping threshold (ε_high).

The "Clip Higher" technique allows the probability ratio (new policy / old policy) to increase more for advantageous actions before being clipped(just like kl_beta=0.0).

Thank you to the authors for their excellent work!Here are some issues we have encountered.

title: Question of the post-training motivatioin.
body:
Hi, thanks for your work. The demo on Hugging-Face is charming.

I am using Qwen-2.5-VL family for object detection these days, both 3B / 7B / 72B demonstrate strong visual positioning capabilities. I ask for the bounding box coordinates of the target object and make it arranged on .json format. After several rounds of prompt word engineering, I can get promising results from the model. Normally this is not a regular VL task, but the Qwen does really well.

So what I'm curious about is whether the SFT and R1 training strategies you mentioned are essentially "how to automatically organize prompts to make object recognition tasks easier", which I mean the automatically prompt engineering, but no new knowledge emerged for the bbox-style detection task?

Looking forward to hearing your answer.
author: doubleZ0108

comments.body:
The current results we show is training the model with only a few hundreds steps on the REC task, so we believe it's more like aligning the model to the task better with GRPO loss (i.e. not much new knowledge is introduced to the model). 

That said the parameters are updated via GRPO training, and when we training the model longer with more tasks, we do believe new knowledge can be injected.
It's an interesting finding. I'll keep an eye on the project.

I ‘m not clear about the specific meaning of the ”normalized solution“ field. Hope you can help me, thanks!
author: CaptainEven

comments.body:
The "normalized_solution" field represents the bounding box coordinates of the target object, scaled relative to the image's width and height. 

Top-left x-coordinate: 103.93 / 427 ≈ 0.243
Top-left y-coordinate: 299.99 / 640 ≈ 0.468 
...

This normalization allows models to recognize and process objects consistently, regardless of image size.

Yeah, @posede 's explanation is right. Since a lot of VLMs output bbox in a normalized form, such as LLaVA, InternVL, we keep this key for future use.
In our setting, we set the max value as 1000. For example, the point (1000, 1000) denotes the bottom-right corner of the image, and the point (0, 1000) denotes the bottom-left corner of the image.
